description: POSITIVE CONTROL. The demo jeopardy board the whole matrix leans on: 5 columns x 5 cells, valueLadder [100..500] per column, one per-cell value override on the lockValue cell (4:4), six randomizable cells, and _note comments at the root and at two nested levels to prove comment-stripping. Must validate clean and render.

POSITIVE CONTROL. Uniform 5x5 bingo card with a preMarked centre free space at cell key 2:2. No valueLadder anywhere, which is correct: bingo requires only `prompt`, scores nothing, and wins on a pattern.

POSITIVE CONTROL. Ranked-list survey board, one column (plan Q11: ranked-list renders ONE column of answer rows). Column label is the survey question; six answers with descending invented point values. Strikes and steals are host-mediated and not modeled.
POSITIVE CONTROL. grid / [hidden,revealed,answered] / accumulate with allowNegative / highest-score / bonus 1 at x2 / uniformRows false / requiredCellFields [prompt,answer,value].

POSITIVE CONTROL. grid / [hidden,marked] / scoring none / pattern-complete with all four patterns / uniformRows TRUE / requiredCellFields [prompt]. `bonus` is omitted on purpose, to exercise DEFAULTS.bonus.
POSITIVE CONTROL. ranked-list / [hidden,revealed] / accumulate without negatives / highest-score / bonus 0 / requiredCellFields [answer,value].
POSITIVE CONTROL. Two-entry manifest: default -> default.css, midnight -> midnight.css. Only files listed here may ever load.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the export/import round trip. gameHash is the real SHA-256 of games/demo.json as authored; re-run `shasum -a 256 games/demo.json` and update it if that file changes. All cellStates keys are inside the demo 5x5 census, all values are in jeopardy's lifecycle, and bonusCells references a randomizable (never lockValue) cell. Carries appVersion, exercising delta D6.

SYNTAX. Trailing comma after the last cell object. Not valid JSON and must never be 'fixed' - the runner fetches it as raw text. errors.js locates it with its own scanner (plan Q6); the browser's JSON.parse message is never inspected. path must be null, location must carry line/column/snippet/caret.
SYNTAX. The `cells` array is never closed - its `]` is missing. Not valid JSON, by design. path null, location set.
SYNTAX. The second cell's `answer` string value is missing its closing double quote, so the string runs to end of file. Not valid JSON, by design. path null, location set.

FETCH. Generated file of ~1.05 MB, over the 1 MB content cap. Padding lives in an unknown `_bulk` key, so if the byte cap were removed the file would validate clean - its size is the only fault. The cap must be checked on the raw bytes BEFORE JSON.parse.

FETCH. gameType is "jepardy", a typo of a shipped id. Well-formed against PATTERNS.gameTypeId, so it survives the structural stage and becomes a path; gametypes/jepardy.json 404s. The failure is reported against the GAME-TYPE file, kind 'gametype', with found 'HTTP 404'.

FETCH. gameType is "wheel-of-fortune": a well-formed id for a game type that was never authored. Same class as unknown-gametype.json and deliberately so - the app cannot distinguish a misspelled name from an uncreated one, and per spec section 5 a 404 on a game-type file IS a validation failure, not a crash.
STRUCTURAL. First cell's `value` is the string "500" where a whole number is required. found must read as a human phrase - 'the string "500"' - not a bare type name.
STRUCTURAL. The required top-level `title` is absent. A top-level field was chosen so the reported path is unambiguous; the nested case is missing-cell-field.json.

STRUCTURAL. schemaVersion is 2, which this build does not implement. Spec section 4.1 forbids best-effort parsing, so validation must STOP here and emit exactly one failure - even though the board below would otherwise validate. expected should be built from supportedVersions('content').

STRUCTURAL. Generated prompt of exactly 2001 characters, one over the 2,000 cap. Also the regression test for the 120-character truncation of `found`: an untruncated 2,001-character phrase would blow out the error screen.

STRUCTURAL. Generated column label of exactly 81 characters, one over the 80-character label cap. The cap covers the whole label class (column labels, game title, team names); the column label stands in for the class.
STRUCTURAL. 13 columns against a cap of 12. Every individual column is valid and every cell states its own value, so the columns array is the only fault.

STRUCTURAL. 13 cells in one column against a cap of 12. There is deliberately no valueLadder: a 13-entry ladder would breach its own 12-item cap and give the file a second fault, so each cell states its own value.

STRUCTURAL, not contract - note the difference from unknown-theme.json. `animation` is "explode". The animation node in schemas.js carries an enum of ANIMATIONS, so a bad name dies structurally and CROSS_CHECKS.animationExists is never reached for a plain unknown name.

STRUCTURAL, kind state. The first team's `score` is the string "400". Identical in shape to valid-state.json apart from that one value, so it is the exact A/B for the import path. Imported state is untrusted input (spec sections 4.4 and 6.6): a corrupted export must land on the error screen, never on a half-restored board.

CONTRACT. The second cell has no `answer`, and jeopardy's requiredCellFields is [prompt,answer,value]. Cells carry no structural `required` list at all - schemas.js says so explicitly, because bingo cells need no prompt - so this can only be caught by cross-checking the game type. The cell's `value` is supplied by the ladder, so `answer` is the single fault.

CONTRACT. theme is "neon-dreams", not a key in themes/themes.json. The name is well-formed, so it passes the structural pattern and dies at the contract stage. Themes load ONLY via the manifest (spec section 6.4) - an unlisted name must never become a <link href>.

CONTRACT. Under gameType bingo, gridConstraints.uniformRows is true. Columns 0 and 1 hold four cells; column 2 holds three. Spec section 4.2: validation fails ragged bingo boards. No valueLadder anywhere, which is not a second fault - bingo requires no values.

CONTRACT, plan Q8. Five cells, a four-entry valueLadder, and the fifth cell carries no per-cell `value`. That is an ERROR, not a silent zero: a board with an invisible missing point value is exactly what the error screen exists to prevent. Cells 0-3 are ladder-covered, so there is precisely one uncovered cell and precisely one failure.
